2_Introduction: The device achieves a notably enhanced PCE of 25.3045%, corresponding to a JSC of 26.403 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.1605 V, and an FF of 82.5803%.  The Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0 (1.65 mol/L) perovskite precursor solution was prepared. For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. At the last 15 s, 150 µL of anti-solvent was rapidly dropped on top of the spinning substrate. Then the film was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₅FA₀.₉PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—engineered with a precisely tuned A-site cationic composition (FA⁺ dominant, supplemented by small fractions of MA⁺ and Cs⁺ to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.985 and suppress δ-phase formation while mitigating halide vacancy-mediated ion migration)—undergoes controlled crystallization via a two-step spin-coating protocol wherein the initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 5 s) step ensures uniform wet-film coverage and interfacial contact with the underlying charge transport layer, followed by high-speed (5500 rpm, 30 s) shear-driven solvent removal that governs nucleation density and grain boundary distribution; critically, the antisolvent quenching at the 15-s mark—delivered as 150 µL of chlorobenzene—triggers instantaneous supersaturation, promoting rapid, homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening and thereby yielding large, oriented grains with reduced intragrain strain and suppressed PbI₂ residual phase, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of the 12.6° PbI₂ peak and narrow (110) FWHM (<0.12°), indicative of low microstrain and high crystallinity; this structural perfection is further reflected in optical characterization, where PL mapping reveals spatially uniform, high-intensity emission across the entire film with negligible dark spots—quantitatively confirming sub-10⁹ cm⁻³ non-radiative defect density—and time-resolved PL exhibits a biexponential decay dominated by a long-lived component (τ₁ ≈ 1.24 µs), signifying suppressed trap-assisted recombination and extended carrier diffusion length; simultaneously, the stoichiometric precision (1.65 mol/L precursor concentration) and thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min enable full conversion of intermediate solvates without inducing halide segregation or organic cation decomposition, thus preserving phase purity and interfacial energetic alignment. Collectively, these synergistic crystallization controls—spanning cation engineering, kinetic nucleation modulation, and thermodynamic stabilization—yield a morphologically continuous, optically coherent, and structurally robust perovskite absorber with minimized bulk and interfacial defects, enabling efficient charge extraction, suppressed voltage losses, and minimal series resistance, culminating in a VOC of 1.1605 V, a JSC of 26.403 mA/cm², an FF of 82.5803%, and a PCE of 25.3045%.
